Estimate divergence time for ancestral nodes

Source: R/inferDivergenceTimes.R
inferDivergenceTimes.Rd

This method infers the divergence time of ancestral nodes based on the information from TimeTree when available, and by extrapolating this information to other nodes without this information when possible.

Usage

inferDivergenceTimes(
  tree,
  timelines = NULL,
  cladeName = NULL,
  savePlots = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  models = c("t_gamdec", "t_lin", "t_scam", "t_exp", "t_gam", "t_iso")
)

Arguments

tree

A ConvenientTblTree object.

timelines

An optional named list of data frames, where each name corresponds to an NCBI ID. Each element in the list is a data frame containing the timeline from the specified taxon to the last common ancestor of all cellular organisms. Each row of the dataframe represents one ancestral node. This list is computed by this function and returned in timeTreeTimelines, but because computation can take time, a previously computed list can also be given as an optional argument.

cladeName

An optional parameter with the name of the analyzed clade.

savePlots

Boolean flag (optional; default value is FALSE). If TRUE, the function saves .png and .svg files containing several plots (e.g. relationship between cumulative branch length and divergence time, stats about the nodes for each path from tip to root, etc.)

verbose

Boolean flag (optional; default value is FALSE). If TRUE, the function prints messages about the computation and summary statistics for the dataset.

models

An optional parameter defining which models will be used for extrapolating the data from TimeTree. Models must be listed in order of preference. The first model is preferred for setting the divergence time. If there is insufficient information to use a model, the next model is tried, and so on. Available options: t_gam (Generalized Additive Model),t_scam (Shape Constrained Additive Model), t_gamdec (Generalized Additive Model with a decreasing monotonicity constraint), t_iso (Isotonic regression), t_lin (Linear interpolation), t_exp (Exponential model),t_power (Power-law model).

Value

A named list with the following information: 1. tree: A ConvenientTblTree object with the following additional columns: divergenceTime (the estimated divergence time for the node, either coming from TimeTree or extrapolated from TimeTree information), isTimeExtrapolated (FALSE if the divergence time comes directly from TimeTree, TRUE if it is extrapolated from TimeTree), cumBranchLen (the sum of the edge lengths from the root to the node), isSingleSpecies (TRUE if all tips share the same NCBI_id; false otherwise), plus additional columns, one per model used, named after the model and containing the divergence times inferred by that model. 2. timeTreeTimelines: A list of data frames, where each name corresponds to an NCBI ID (from column NCBI_id). Each element in the list is a data frame containing the timeline from the specified taxon to the last common ancestor of all cellular organisms. Each row of the dataframe represents one ancestral node. 3. timeTreeDivergenceTimes: A named list of data frames, where each element corresponds to an ancestral node in the tree for which a divergence time is available from TimeTree (names correspond to column node). Each element has a dataframe (computed with the function inferDivTimesFromTimeTree), with one row per informative pair of leaves and the divergence time inferred from that pair. Notice that an ancestral node may have multiple pairs of leaves that yield different divergence times, indicating a possible disagreement between the TimeTree phylogeny and the phylogeny from ScrambledTreeBuilder. 4. pathsLeafToRoot: All paths from tips to root used for the divergence time estimation, sorted by the amount of information from TimeTree they have.

Note

See functions model_gam (option t_gam), model_scam (option t_scam), model_gamdec (t_gamdec), model_iso (option t_iso), model_lin (option t_lin), model_exp (option t_exp), model_power (option t_power) for more details on each model.
